description: Design or review an Azure HIPAA-minded API surface for workloads that ingest, store, or disclose electronic protected health information (ePHI). This pattern helps teams document how Azure API Management (APIM) exposes HTTPS-only, policy-governed routes; App Service workloads run integrated with your virtual network so private subnets reach Azure SQL without advertising the database on the internet; and Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) on Azure SQL satisfies encryption-at-rest expectations that HIPAA Security Rule reviewers routinely ask auditors to demonstrate. Naming APIM + VNet integration + SQL TDE in the footprint makes minimum-necessary segmentation, PHI boundary drawings, and BAA-aligned subprocess contracts easier to articulate to assessors—even though HIPAA is ultimately organizational and procedural, not purely technical.
constraints: Azure SQL logical server never accepts traffic from arbitrary public IPs; connectivity only via private endpoints or VNet-integrated data paths reviewed with security stakeholders.
All client-to-api traffic enters through Azure API Management with TLS enforced; APIM serves as explicit policy choke point for quotas, JWT validation, and audit-friendly routing metadata.
TDE must remain enabled on every Azure SQL database holding or potentially holding ePHI; key ownership (service-managed vs customer-managed) decided with compliance sign-off.
requiredCapabilities: Azure API Management as the external API façade with logging and policy layers suitable for access review evidence
Azure App Service with VNet integration (or equivalent private egress) for application tier isolation
Azure SQL Database with TDE enabled and documented backup/restore retention aligned to policy
Entra ID or equivalent for workforce and machine identity with conditional access for privileged roles
assumptions: Business Associate Agreements cover Azure as a subprocessor where ePHI transits or rests in the listed services.
Audit logging for API access and schema changes is centralized (e.g., Log Analytics) with retention meeting policy.
topologyHints: North-south: internet -> APIM -> private App Service -> private Azure SQL; document each hop for HIPAA risk analysis.
Separate non-production environments from production PHI; mask or synthetic data only in lower environments unless exception is approved.
securityBaselineHints: Document minimum necessary access for APIM operators, App Service deployment principals, and SQL admin roles.
Defender for Cloud and Azure Policy checks on public exposure, weak TLS, and missing private endpoints support HIPAA audit narratives.
